instrument_name: Improved Workforce Opportunity Wage Act, 2018 PA 337 as amended by 2025 PA 1 (MCL 408.931-408.945), compiled through PA 114 of 2026
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum hourly wage 12.48 from 2025-02-21; 13.73 from 2026-01-01; 15.00 from 2027-01-01 (enacted). From October 2027 the State Treasurer indexes by 12-month Midwest CPI-U, published by 1 November, effective 1 January following; no increase if MI unemployment >= 8.5% the preceding year. Employer = 2+ employees; employee = 16 years or older. Act does not apply to FLSA-covered employers unless the federal minimum is lower (408.940(1)); companionship and non-live-in childcare workers covered (408.940(2)).

instrument_name: Improved Workforce Opportunity Wage Act sec. 4a overtime and compensatory time (MCL 408.934a)
figure_or_rule_carried: Overtime 1.5x regular rate over 40 hours in a workweek; public hospital 8/80 option by written agreement; exemptions: bona fide executive/administrative/professional, seasonal amusement (<=7 months), agriculture, employees not subject to the minimum wage. Compensatory time in lieu of overtime at 1.5 hours per hour, cap 240 hours, cash out within 30 days of request, unused comp time paid at termination; comp time earned/paid must appear on the statement of earnings (408.934a(8)(d)(ii)). Civil fine up to 1,000.

instrument_name: Improved Workforce Opportunity Wage Act secs. 4b and 4d: training, minor and tipped minimum wages (MCL 408.934b, 408.934d)
figure_or_rule_carried: Training wage 4.25/hour for first 90 days, new employee under 20; under-18 minimum = 85% of general minimum (2026: 13.73 x 0.85 = 11.6705, derived). Tipped minimum = % of general minimum: 38% from 2025-02-21, 40% from 2026-01-01 (13.73 x 0.40 = 5.492, derived), 42% 2027, 44% 2028, 46% 2029, 48% 2030, 50% 2031; conditions: tips cover the gap, FICA-declared, retained by employee (pooling only in chain of service), written notice and written consent at hire; service-charge distribution notice; records 3 years after last pay period; civil fine up to 2,500.

instrument_name: Earned Sick Time Act, 2018 PA 338 as amended by 2025 PA 2 (MCL 408.961-408.974), compiled through PA 114 of 2026
figure_or_rule_carried: Every employer (1+ employees). Accrual 1 hour per 30 hours worked (PTO hours excluded). Small business (10 or fewer working in a week; not small if >10 on payroll in 20+ workweeks of current/prior year): usage cap 40 hours/year, carry-over cap 40, or frontload 40; small-business obligations start 2025-10-01. Others: usage cap 72 hours/year, carry-over cap 72, or frontload 72; part-time proportional frontload with written notice of expected hours. Exempt (FLSA 13(a)(1)) employees assumed 40 h/week. Pay at greater of normal hourly/base wage or state minimum (overtime, holiday pay, bonuses, commissions, piece rate, tips excluded). Use in 1-hour or smallest increment; new hires may be made to wait 120 calendar days. Frontloading employers need not carry over, track or pay out. Not paid out at separation (408.965(3)); rehire within 2 months reinstates unused balance unless paid out. PTO policy of equal amount complies. Excluded: federal employees, self-scheduling workers, unpaid interns, youth-employment-standards minors. Records of hours worked and sick time 3 years (408.970). Civil fine up to 8x normal hourly wage; posting violation up to 100.

instrument_name: Payment of Wages and Fringe Benefits Act, 1978 PA 390, sec. 2 (MCL 408.472) pay frequency and timing
figure_or_rule_carried: Default semi-monthly: wages for days 1-15 paid by the 1st of the next month; days 16-end paid by the 15th of the next month. Weekly or biweekly regular payday complies if payday is on or before the 14th day after the end of the work period. Monthly pay period complies if paid within 15 days after period end. December overtime may be paid on the next regular payday. Hand harvesters: by the 2nd day after the work week. Employer = 1+ employees.

instrument_name: Payment of Wages and Fringe Benefits Act sec. 6 (MCL 408.476) method of payment: direct deposit and payroll debit card
figure_or_rule_carried: Methods: cash; negotiable check payable without discount; direct deposit/electronic transfer; payroll debit card meeting (6). Direct deposit and paycard need full, free, written consent, EXCEPT employer may mandate direct deposit or paycard if it gives a written election form (DD or paycard), a statement that failure to return the form within 30 days = consent to paycard (not for those already on DD), and paycard disclosures (fees, free access, ATM charges, free balance, right to change, no bank account). Employee may change method at any time, implemented within 1 pay period. Paycard: 1 free withdrawal per pay period, 21 days notice of fee changes, unlimited free balance inquiries, no credit link. Employer may not pass payment-method costs to the employee.

instrument_name: Payment of Wages and Fringe Benefits Act secs. 3-5 and 10 (MCL 408.473-408.475, 408.480) final pay, fringe benefits (vacation), deceased employee
figure_or_rule_carried: Final pay: voluntary quit - all wages earned and due as soon as the amount can with due diligence be determined (hand harvesters: within 3 days); discharge - immediately, as soon as the amount can with due diligence be determined; contract workers - estimated wages per sec. 2, final payment at contract end. Fringe benefits (holiday, sick, personal, vacation, bonuses, expenses, contributions) are paid per the written contract or written policy (408.471(e), 408.473): accrued-vacation payout at termination follows the written policy, no statutory payout. Fringe benefit due at termination may be withheld only by written contract or signed free consent (408.474). Deceased employee: wages/fringe to written designee if no letters of administration, else spouse, children, parents, siblings in that order; payment discharges the employer.

instrument_name: Payment of Wages and Fringe Benefits Act sec. 7 (MCL 408.477) wage deductions
figure_or_rule_carried: No deduction without full, free, written consent except those required/expressly permitted by law or CBA. Deduction for the employer benefit: written consent for EACH wage payment and may not take gross below the state minimum wage (charitable deductions to a 501(c)(3) employer: one consent). Each deduction substantiated per employee; no prorating. Overpayment recovery without consent within 6 months if clerical/math error, written explanation 1 pay period before, max 15% of gross for the period, taken after all other deductions, not below the greater of state/FLSA minimum. Same 15% rule for an employer-paid default judgment under MCL 600.4012(9)/(10). Complaint within 12 months.

instrument_name: Payment of Wages and Fringe Benefits Act sec. 9 (MCL 408.479) records and wage statement; IWOWA sec. 7 (MCL 408.937)
figure_or_rule_carried: Record per employee: name, address, birth date, occupation/classification, total basic rate of pay, total hours each pay period, total wages each pay period, separate itemization of deductions, listing of fringe benefits; kept 3 years. Statement at time of payment: hours worked, gross wages paid, pay period identification, separate itemization of deductions (piece-rate hand harvesters: units). Hours need not be recorded/stated for bona fide executive, administrative, professional employees, elected officials, political appointees. Statute is silent on electronic delivery (no consent rule located). IWOWA 408.937 repeats: statement of hours, wages and deductions each pay period. Re-read of the act text; complements US-MI-P5-1-005 / US-MIL-002.

instrument_name: Michigan Employment Security Act sec. 44 (MCL 421.44) remuneration, wages and taxable wage limit
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable wage limit 9,500 per employee per calendar year; reduced to 9,000 for the whole year for non-delinquent employers when the fund balance on 30 June of the prior year is >= 2.5 billion and projected to stay there (statutory mechanism behind the 2026 9,000 base in US-MI-P5-1-004; delinquent = quarterly unpaid balance >= 25, cured if paid within 45 days of the first quarter). Not indexed (fixed amounts). Wages include FICA-reported tips; wages paid by the same employer in other states count toward the limit; successor counts predecessor wages. Excluded from wages: retirement/sickness/medical plan payments, 401(a)/403(a) trust payments, employer-paid employee FICA, non-cash pay outside the trade or business, deductible moving expenses, SUB plan payments, National Guard pay. Remuneration not received within 21 days after period end deemed paid on day 21.

instrument_name: Michigan Employment Security Act sec. 43 (MCL 421.43) services excluded from employment (UI coverage of special populations)
figure_or_rule_carried: Excluded from UI employment: H-2A agricultural aliens; agricultural labor unless the employer meets sec. 41(5); domestic service in a private home unless employer meets sec. 41(6); service for son, daughter or spouse and child under 18 for a parent; commission-only real estate, investment and insurance agents; 501(c)(3)-type exempt orgs if under 50 in the quarter; students employed by their school (normally <=30 h/week) and spouses with notice; under-22 co-op students in a certified program; newspaper delivery under 18; for-profit employers: minor students below college level working less than scheduled hours / in school vacations / in accredited curriculum, college students in accredited curriculum; direct sellers; product demonstrators meeting the test; AmeriCorps; landmen. Church employment excluded for sec. 42(8)-(10) purposes.

instrument_name: Michigan Employment Security Act sec. 19 (MCL 421.19) contribution rates: new and construction employers
figure_or_rule_carried: New employer rate 2.7% in years 1 and 2 of liability (then phased in with the chargeable benefits component in years 3-4/5); construction employers pay the average construction contractor rate determined by the agency in years 1-2, then phased. Rate components (CBC, ABC, NBC) as in US-MIP9W-002. Statutory basis for the 2.7% in US-MI-P5-1-003; employer-only contributions (no employee UI contribution in MI: US-FED-P5-2-006 lists AK, NJ, PA only).

instrument_name: Social Security Number Privacy Act, 2004 PA 454 (MCL 445.81-445.87)
figure_or_rule_carried: A person may not intentionally publicly display, print on badges/cards, use as primary account number, transmit over an unsecured connection, or include visibly through an envelope, all or more than 4 sequential digits of an SSN; mailing a document with more than 4 digits is allowed where law authorises it or to service an employee benefit. Uses authorised or required by federal/state law (e.g. W-2) are exempt. Anyone obtaining SSNs in the ordinary course of business must adopt and publish (handbook/manual, may be electronic) a privacy policy: confidentiality, no unlawful disclosure, access limits, disposal, penalties. Payroll effect: pay statement shows at most the last 4 digits.

instrument_name: Local Government Labor Regulatory Limitation Act, 2015 PA 105 (MCL 123.1381-123.1396)
figure_or_rule_carried: Local governments may not require a minimum wage above the state minimum, local prevailing wage/fringe rates (except state projects), paid or unpaid leave, or hours/scheduling rules (ordinances adopted after 2014-12-31). Payroll effect: no local minimum wage or local paid-leave layer in Michigan; the state minimum (US-MIS5-001) and ESTA (US-MIS5-004) are the only rates.

instrument_name: Income Tax Act of 1967 sec. 30 (MCL 206.30) taxable income, personal exemption indexation, tips and overtime deduction (subdiv. (ee) added by 2025 PA 24; compiled through 2026 PA 39)
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable income starts from federal AGI (rolling IRC conformity, so federal exclusions such as 401(k) deferrals, sec. 125, HSA, transit and group-term life flow through), with listed adjustments. Personal exemption base 3,700 indexed annually by US CPI for the state fiscal year ending in the prior tax year over FY2010-11, plus 600 from 2022, rounded to the nearest 100 (2026 value 5,900 per Guide 446). NEW: subdiv. (ee), enacted by 2025 PA 24 (signed 2025-10-07, per Treasury notice US-MIS5-017): tax years 2026-2028 deduct federally allowed qualified tips (IRC 224) and qualified overtime (IRC 225), nonresidents only for MI-sourced amounts. Level = ASSESSMENT (individual return); no withholding change located in statute, Guide 446 Rev. 02-26 or the Treasury notice. Section last amended by 2026 PA 39, imd. eff. 2026-07-22 (content of that amendment not isolated). (ff): from TY2025 AGI computed decoupled from IRC 168(n)/174A.

instrument_name: Support and Parenting Time Enforcement Act, 1982 PA 295, sec. 8 (MCL 552.608) limit on support income withholding
figure_or_rule_carried: Total income withheld under all support withholding orders (current support, arrears, fees, health-care premiums) may not exceed 50% of disposable earnings as defined in 15 USC 1672 (a flat state cap, lower than the CCPA 55/60/65% tiers for some cases).

instrument_name: Michigan Treasury Taxpayer Notice: New Deductions for Qualified Overtime Compensation and Qualified Tips (2026-01-06)
authority: Michigan Department of Treasury, Bureau of Tax Policy
article_or_section: Notice, sections Background / Tax Years Impacted / Implementation
figure_or_rule_carried: 2025 PA 24, signed 2025-10-07, amended MCL 206.30 (subdiv. (ee)): deduction of federally deducted qualified tips (IRC 224) and qualified overtime (IRC 225) for tax years 2026, 2027, 2028 only (not 2025); residents deduct all, nonresidents only amounts attributable to services in Michigan. Status: ENACTED, in force. Level: ASSESSMENT (taxable income on MI-1040); the notice contains no employer withholding instruction; further guidance may be issued. A tier-B search summary claiming employers must stop MI withholding on tips is NOT supported by this notice or Guide 446 Rev. 02-26.

instrument_name: Michigan Treasury 2026 Sales, Use and Withholding Taxes Monthly/Quarterly Return (Form 5080, Rev. 12-25) and Annual Return (Form 5081, Rev. 04-25), from the 2026 Withholding Tax Forms page
figure_or_rule_carried: Withholding is reported on the combined SUW return (one frequency for all SUW tax types on the account, assigned by Treasury): Form 5080 monthly/quarterly return due the 20th of the month following the return period; Form 5081 annual return for 2026 due 2027-02-28, reconciling total W-2/1099 count (line 17), MI tax withheld per W-2/1099 (line 18) and withholding paid (line 19a); do not attach W-2s. Late penalty 5% of tax due (+interest). Filing via MTO, approved software or paper; payments by MTO, EFT credit (Form 2329) or voucher 5094. Forms page also lists MI-W4, MI W-4P, 447 (magnetic media transmittal), 151 POA, 163 discontinuance, 3281 new hire form. Filing-frequency thresholds (incl. accelerated/EFT) NOT stated on these documents.

instrument_name: Michigan Form MI-W4 Employee Withholding Exemption Certificate (Rev. 12-20) with Guide 446 (Rev. 02-26) MI-W4 rules
figure_or_rule_carried: State certificate MI-W4 required; federal W-4 cannot substitute. Line 6 number of personal and dependency exemptions (cannot exceed MI-1040 entitlement); line 7 additional amount per pay (if employer agrees); line 8a/8b exemption from withholding (no liability; nonresident military spouse; other exempt reasons); line 5 new-hire date. No certificate = withhold on zero exemptions. Invalid/altered certificate: ignore, require new one, keep prior valid one. Employer sends copies to Treasury (Tax Technical Section, PO Box 30477) when 10+ exemptions or exempt claimed, not for reciprocal-state residents. Per-period withholding = 4.25% x (wages - exemptions x 5,900 / pay periods) (Guide 446). Nonresidency: employer-designed certificate/letter (Treasury issues none).

instrument_name: Michigan UIA Employer FAQ - Quarterly Reports (MiUI)
article_or_section: FAQ: When are quarterly reports due? / How do I complete and submit
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer Quarterly Wage/Tax Report filed in MiUI (File a Report; corrections via Wage Detail Reporting > Wage Adjustments). Due 25 January, 25 April, 25 July, 25 October; if the 25th is a weekend/holiday, next business day. MiUI Release 1 (Tax) go-live 2026-02-23 per US-MI-P5-1-004. File format/specification for bulk wage files not read (see MiUI quarterly wage report testing page, open question).

instrument_name: Michigan Treasury Withholding Tax page (Due Dates) and Accelerated EFT Filers page
figure_or_rule_carried: Treasury assigns monthly, quarterly or annual frequency each year; monthly due the 20th of the following month; quarterly due 20 April / 20 July / 20 October / 20 January; annual 28 February following year; all filers also file the annual return by 28 February. Weekend/state holiday: next business day. Accelerated EFT: withholding liability of 480,000 or more in the previous calendar year (sales/use 720,000) -> withholding remitted by EFT (credit or debit) on or before the same day as the federal deposit, regardless of amount; Treasury notifies in April, change effective July. Withholding calculator listed under Estimators and Calculators (oracle: www.michigan.gov/taxes/business-taxes/withholding/tax-calculator per Guide 446).

instrument_name: Michigan UIA MiUI Quarterly Wage Report file format reference documents (Delimited v3, EFW2 v2, ICESA v2, XML v1; 2026 specifications) and Quarterly Wage Report Testing page
article_or_section: File Format Specifications; Record tables; Document Change Logs
figure_or_rule_carried: After MiUI launch, quarterly wage reports (current and past due) are submitted in MiUI in one of four formats: Delimited CSV (.txt/.csv), ICESA (NASWA, .txt), EFW2 (formerly MMREF-SSA, .txt, fixed 512-byte records, Employer Header RE + Employee Detail RS, many SSA fields Not Used by MI UIA), XML (.xml). Legacy MiWAM file format no longer accepted. Change logs: 2026 v1 2026-02-23; Delimited v2 2026-03-30 (EAN max length 10 -> 7), v3 2026-04-08 (blank/0 Obligation Gross Wages); EFW2 v2 2026-04-03 (blank Out of State Wages). Reporting unit 000 = main company. Wage Report Validator Tool for tests (no live PII).

instrument_name: Michigan Prevailing Wages on State Projects, 2023 PA 10 as amended by 2024 PA 110 (MCL 408.1101-408.1122): certified payroll and records
figure_or_rule_carried: Scope: state projects (construction etc. authorised by a public contracting agent and state-financed in whole or part) and, from 2025-04-02, private energy facility projects (solar/wind >= 2 MW, storage). No dollar threshold in the act. Contractors and subcontractors need a state project registration (sec. 2a, 2024 PA 110). Pay construction mechanics not less than locality prevailing wage and fringe rates; post rates on site; keep record of name, occupation, actual wages and benefits. Certified payroll records kept 3 years and transmitted within 10 days after the end of each pay period (to the contracting agent, then from 1 year after 2024 PA 110 to the LEO certified-payroll database): classification, apprentice/journeyman level, gross wages, hours per day, start/end times, hourly, overtime and fringe rates; no home address, phone or SSN in the database; e-signed attestation. Civil fine up to 5,000 per violation. Detail read on the local copy behind US-MI-P5-1-006.

instrument_name: Office of Child Support Act, 1971 PA 174, sec. 6 (MCL 400.236) State Disbursement Unit
figure_or_rule_carried: The Michigan State Disbursement Unit (MiSDU) is the single location to which a payer or source of income (employer) sends withheld support and fee payments; SDU disburses within 2 business days; an NSF payment from the source of income can be collected with expenses. Employer fee for processing an IWO: not located in the sections read (open).

instrument_name: Michigan UIA Employer FAQ - Taxable Wage Base
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable wage base 9,000 for qualified (non-delinquent) employers; delinquent employers do not qualify (9,500). Trigger: Trust Fund >= 2.5 billion on 30 June of the prior year and the next quarter. Page states a new employer at 2.7% saves on average 14.00 per employee: 0.027 x (9,500 - 9,000) = 13.50, rounded on the page to 14 (derivation reconciles the 9,000/9,500 pair with MCL 421.44(4), US-MIS5-010). Payroll systems must set the 2026 taxable wage at 9,000. No 2027 base stated.

instrument_name: MDHHS Office of Child Support - New Hire Reporting (employers)
authority: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services - Office of Child Support
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers must report newly hired or rehired employees to the Office of Child Support through the Michigan New Hires Operation Center, (800) 524-9846, via the Michigan New Hire Reporting website (mi-newhire.com; Form 3281 per Treasury forms list). Page states no deadline, fields or penalty: deadline rests on federal 42 USC 653a 20 days (US-FED-017); Michigan statute not located.
